memory_candidates.content: Lean 4 AppBuilder arity trap in BimodalLogic: mkAppM's Array Expr holds only EXPLICIT arguments, so passing a type for an implicit parameter (e.g. mkAppM ``List.nil #[formulaType]) raises 'too many explicit arguments provided to @List.nil' on every input, including the empty list. The repo contains both the broken instance (FormalSystem/Tactic/Meta.lean buildContextExpr) and a line-for-line correct twin (FormalSystem/Automation/ProofMode/Meta.lean contextExpr) using mkAppOptM ``List.nil #[some type]. Meta.mkListLit (mkConst ``Formula) formulas produces a syntactically identical Expr and is a one-line alternative. A MetaM helper's failure is a runtime elaborator failure, never a compile error, so a #check pins the signature of a function that throws on every call -- only an invoked #eval probe is coverage.

BimodalLogic's package-level weak.linter.mathlibStandardSet rejects a blank line inside a command unless a comment follows it ('Please, write a comment here or remove this line, but do not place empty lines within commands!'). Consequence when refactoring a Lean do-block: moving a statement and its explanatory comment together can leave a legal-looking blank line that newly trips this linter, failing a zero-warning gate. Invisible to review; only a compiled lake build surfaces it.

Research-phase working-tree probe discipline on BimodalLogic's shared tree: to compile-verify a candidate repair during research, copy the target files to the session scratchpad first, patch in place, build through lake-build-guard.sh, then restore from the saved copies and confirm with md5sum plus an empty 'git diff -- <dirs>'. Do NOT use 'git checkout -- <path>' to revert: guard-destructive-git.sh blocks the pathspec-discard form whenever the tree is dirty at all, which it routinely is when other sessions hold uncommitted specs/ changes. Also run the counterfactual build (repair reverted, test kept) to prove the new test actually discriminates rather than passing vacuously.
